newsitem.title: IRAQ: Saddam rails at U.S. and allies on war anniversary.
newsitem.headline: Saddam rails at U.S. and allies on war anniversary.

text.p: Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein marked the sixth anniversary on Friday of the start of the Gulf War with a tirade against the United States and its allies.
In a speech broadcast on Iraqi radio and television, Saddam, dressed in military uniform, likened the allied forces to the "front of Satans".
Then U.S. president George Bush was "the leader of the group of vice and aggression", Saddam said.
He blasted the U.N. trade sanctions imposed on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait and said enemies were prolonging them as a means to "annihilate" the Iraqi people.

Saddam, referring to international weapons experts acting under Gulf War ceasefire terms, said Iraq's weapons were being dismantled but they could not kill "the Iraqis' will, steadfastness, patience, faith and their extended optimism for a great and glorious future for them and their glorified nation."

Saddam made no mention of what course Iraq intended to take in its relations with the outside world following implementation of an oil-for-food deal with the United Nations allowing limited oil exports.

The start of the war, in which Iraqi forces were driven from Kuwait, is being celebrated as a national day in Iraq. Official newspapers praised the "mother of battles" and state radio and television broadcast national songs.
